title: Intraoperative and Postoperative Intensive Care in Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery Patients - A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study
summary:
Epilepsy surgery is an established treatment option for children with medically intractable epilepsy and, in appropriately selected patients, can result in a substantial reduction in seizure frequency or even complete seizure freedom. Following surgery, pediatric patients are frequently admitted to an intensive care unit for close monitoring and the early detection and management of potential postoperative complications. However, the actual incidence and nature of complications requiring intensive care remain incompletely characterized.

This multicenter retrospective cohort study aims to evaluate the frequency and nature of anaesthesiologic and intensive care complications occurring after pediatric epilepsy surgery. In addition, we aim to identify perioperative risk factors associated with these complications. The findings may help to better determine which children require routine postoperative intensive care unit admission after epilepsy surgery.

We will conduct a retrospective chart review of children and adolescents who underwent epilepsy surgery involving craniotomy at high-volume epilepsy centers in Germany between 2000 and 2025.

interventions.name: Retrospective chart review enrolling patients with medically intractable epilepsy who underwent epilepsy surgery involving craniotomy at high-volume epilepsy centers between 2000 and 2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age <18 years at time of surgery.
Epilepsy surgery including resective and non-resective procedures involving craniotomy performed at one of the participating centers during the study period (2000-2025).
Exclusion criteria:
Any interventions not involving craniotomy, e.g. stereotactic interventions, placement of sudural grid or strip electrodes, stereotactic laser or radiofrequency ablations).
Surgery involving craniotomy not involved to underlying epileptic disorders.
Patients transferred from other institutions for postoperative care (lack of complete intraoperative data)
